alignments.note: Connective δέ rendered by the verse-opening And.

Inflected verb takes its supplied subject I and its supplied object you (italicized in the ASV); rule 74 keeps a supplied object with the verb that requires it in English, and rule 11 keeps the italics from making it added. Head on the lexical verb exhort per rule 9.

the more exceedingly renders the single comparative adverb; no Greek article stands here, so the degree the and the comparative more are rule 7 helpers on the adverb. Head on exceedingly, the word glossing the lexeme, not on the first word (rule 17).
No preposition or conjunction governs this infinitive, so the infinitival to is an ordinary rule 7/61 helper on its verb.
Substantival demonstrative object of the infinitive.
Purpose ἵνα realized by the word introducing the English clause (rule 40); here that rather than a bare infinitive.
Aorist passive subjunctive with its supplied subject and the modal/passive auxiliaries; head on the lexical participle restored per rules 9 and 17.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition riding along (rule 21).
the sooner renders the comparative adverb; no Greek article is present, so the is a rule 7 helper on the adverb it determines, headed on sooner.

review_notes: All 9 source and all 19 target ids partitioned exactly once.

Two comparative adverbs (s001, s007) each carry a supplied English the with no Greek article behind it; treated as rule 7 helpers rather than added, and headed on the adverb word rather than on more/the.
The italicized you* (t004) is the supplied object of παρακαλῶ and stays with the verb; reading it as added under rule 11 was considered and rejected, since the verb licenses it.
